vector: RESULTS — a manifest of which rounds have a results file, nothing more. It is NOT the season calendar and must never become one again. The calendar (which rounds exist, in what order, on what dates, with what sessions) is the WEEKEND vector at ../../season/2026/index_weekends.json. Join by SLUG.

verified_note: Every claim in ./README.md was checked against the first NINE round files on 2026-07-28. ⚠️ Rounds 10 (Spa), 11 (Hungaroring), 12 (Zandvoort), 13 (Monza) and 14 (Madring) are NOT covered by that check — re-verify and re-stamp this set. A status line nobody re-reads is worse than none. ⚠️ Round 12 also introduced two shapes the README predates and that a re-verify must rule on: (a) a classification row carrying BOTH a finishing position and status DNF (Albon, classified 17th after retiring on lap 66) — recorded verbatim from formula1.com rather than normalised, and (b) a sprint block holding the FULL classification (22 rows) where rounds 9 and 11 hold only the eight points-scoring positions. Neither is a schema change; both are coverage decisions made deliberately and reversible in one edit. ⚠️ Round 13 omits per-driver fastLap for every row except the overall fastest-lap holder — individual lap times beyond the race's single fastest lap were not primary-source-verified this pass, so they were left out rather than guessed. That is a coverage gap against the Zandvoort precedent, not a schema change. ⚠️ Round 14 follows round 13's fastLap coverage decision deliberately, and adds a THIRD shape the README predates: two drivers (Stroll, Bearman) set no qualifying time at all and are stored with qualifying.pos null rather than an invented position, because the FIA classified them NC. Round 14 also carries a grid value of 22 for Bearman as an explicit REPRESENTATION of a pit-lane start following the round 13 precedent, stated in the row itself — the FIA starting grid lists only 21 cars. A re-verify must rule on whether a null qualifying position and a represented pit-lane grid slot are the conventions going forward.
moved_out_2026_08_01: `round`, `date`, `name`, `sprint` and `cuTaskId` left this file for the weekend vector, and `current_round_slug` / `last_completed_round_slug` are now DERIVED at boot by source/08_season.js. Reason: this file can only ever list rounds that have already been RACED, so it structurally cannot be the calendar — and while it was treated as one, two hand-maintained round numberings drifted apart and stayed wrong for eight months. Decision Log J7-J8. ⚠️ RICKY: the weekly refresh runbook writes `cuTaskId` and advances `current_round_slug`. The first no longer lives here; the second no longer exists. Adding a round is now: write the round file, add ONE {slug, file} row below, done. ⚠️ 2026-09-18: this note is CORRECT and the runbook is the thing that is wrong — f1-refresh.md step 4 still says to write slug/round/name/date/cuTaskId/sprint/file into a file it calls `index.json`, which is neither this filename nor this row shape. Reported in the run report, not patched from inside a refresh.
filename_note: The r<NN> prefix on round files is a LABEL, not a claim. Round numbers are derived from calendar position, so a filename ordinal can only stay true because insertions and cancellations always land in the FUTURE while files only exist for the PAST. That is safe by construction, not by design — never rename a past round file to chase a renumber, and never read the ordinal out of a filename.
